questions.question: In src/impl/tokenParser.js, what does the `match` function return when the input does not match the regex?
questions.answer: It returns `[null, {}]` (i.e., `matches` is `null` and the second element is an empty object).

questions.question: In src/impl/tokenParser.js, what does `dateTimeFromMatches` return for the zone when `matches.Z` is defined?
questions.answer: It returns a `FixedOffsetZone` instance constructed from `matches.Z` (i.e., `new FixedOffsetZone(matches.Z)`).

questions.question: In src/impl/conversions.js, what does hasInvalidWeekData return when obj.weekYear is not an integer?
questions.answer: It returns the Invalid object from unitOutOfRange("weekYear", obj.weekYear).

questions.question: In src/impl/conversions.js, in hasInvalidTimeData, what condition makes hour 24 valid?
questions.answer: Hour 24 is valid only when minute === 0, second === 0, and millisecond === 0.

questions.question: In src/impl/digits.js, what does parseDigits return when the input string contains no parseable digits?
In digitRegex in src/impl/digits.js, what numbering system is used by default when the numberingSystem argument is not provided?
questions.answer: It defaults to 'latn', whose pattern is \d.

questions.question: In src/zone.js, what does the `type` getter of the `Zone` class do?
In src/zone.js, what values does the `format` argument of `formatOffset` accept?
In src/settings.js, what does the Settings.defaultZone getter return when the internal defaultZone variable is null?
In src/settings.js, what does the Settings.defaultZoneName setter do when passed a falsy value such as an empty string?
questions.answer: It sets the internal defaultZone variable to null.

questions.question: In site/demo/demo.js, what does the run function return if the eval call throws an exception?
questions.answer: It logs the error to the console and returns the string "[error]".

questions.question: In site/demo/demo.js, what does the demo function do with the examples array after all example calls?
questions.answer: It joins the examples into an HTML table, prepends a heading and description, and assigns the resulting HTML string to document.body.innerHTML.
